newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani markets see better times after polls.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani markets see better times after polls.

text.p: Pakistani markets reacted positively on Thursday to a Supreme Court ruling that endorsed President Leghari's dismissal of Benazir Bhutto's government and cleared the way for elections to go ahead.
"The market has given the decision a resounding thumbs-up," said Abid Naqvi, head of research at Taurus Securities.

The court's verdict on Wednesday meant national and provincial assembly elections would go ahead on February 3 as scheduled, with Bhutto's arch-foe, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif of the Pakistan Muslim League, a clear front-runner.

Stocks surged in a rally sparked by the decision and hopes of an election win for the industrialist Sharif. The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index had risen 31.08 points, or 2.06 percent, to 1,543.23 by noon.

"Business sentiment is positive overall," said an analyst at a foreign bank, adding that the corporate sector generally believed a Sharif victory might be the best recipe for restoring badly needed political and economic stability.
He said international trade activity had ground to a near-standstill in the past few months. As imports dipped, hedging or forward dollar buying had also decreased.
The analyst, who asked not to be named, said one client representing a big multinational had said his company's expansion plans hung on who would be next prime minister.
Dealers in the interbank forex market said industrial activity was likely to pick up soon after the elections which might stimulate imports and push up the forward dollar premium.
They said the premium on one-month forward dollars rose to 0.37 rupees on Thursday from 0.33 a few days ago and was likely to touch 0.40 rupees after Monday's polls.
In the kerb market, the rupee opened 0.03 up at 42 to the dollar and dealers said it might rise further before the close as investors sold dollars to divert funds to the stock market.

"As political uncertainty ebbs, we can see the dollar edging lower," dealer Owais Kalia of Khanani & Kalia International said. The rupee might surge to 41.75 against the dollar if Sharif took power, he added.
"Nawaz Sharif is the favourite of the market. His victory will mean more investment and more business activity," he said.
Naqvi agreed that perceptions of Sharif as a pro-business politician were likely to cheer the depressed stock market.
"A favourable outcome for Sharif will temporarily lift domestic market gloom and push the index into the 1,700-1,800 point territory," he said.
But a Sharif victory would not change Pakistan's poor economic fundamentals and there was also a danger of instability if losing parties rejected the election result, he said.

Naqvi said the balance of power between Sharif and President Farooq Leghari, the role of the newly-created Council for Defence and National Security, and ratification of ordinances issued by Leghari might all become bones of contention.
"We expect a reality check to end the euphoria fairly soon, with the index trekking down and consolidating at the 1,500-point level," he said.
